## Mr. Stripes — *Friendship is Magic* (G4)

Mr. Stripes is the imposing, overprotective Manehattan landlord who makes Rarity hire his daughter **Plaid Stripes** at her new boutique, *Rarity For You*. Remember him as the purple-moustached stallion in a blue tracksuit who loves miniature doll furniture almost as much as his daughter.

- **Look:** Pale mint-gray Earth pony; short violet mane, heavy eyebrows and moustache, magenta eyes, three pink stars for a cutie mark, blue tracksuit, turquoise towel and gold pendant. The [Friendship is Magic color guide](https://mlpvector.club/cg/pony/v/142-Mr-Stripes) documents his palette.
- **Name and status:** Rarity actually calls him “Mr. Stripes” in the [episode transcript](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Transcripts/The_Saddle_Row_Review), so this is an *on-screen name*, not an invented fandom label. Enterplay's licensed [Series 4 card #29](https://mylittlewiki.org/wiki/Enterplay_Trading_Cards) names him alongside Plaid Stripes; “Pushy Pony” is a descriptive subtitle on [collectible-game card #70](https://mlpccg.fandom.com/wiki/Defenders_of_Equestria), not a separate identity.
- **Speaking/voice:** Yes—several lines, voiced in English by **Alan Marriott**, who also voices reporter Buried Lede in this episode ([cast credits](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt5347354/fullcredits/)).
- **Appearances:** Main role in **“The Saddle Row Review” (S6E9, aired May 21, 2016)**; reused flashback footage in **“A-Dressing Memories”** (*Friendship is Forever* clip-show continuity). The later finale cameo and comic appearances often attributed to “the Stripes” involve *Plaid*, not necessarily her father ([character appearance record](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Mr._Stripes_and_Plaid_Stripes); [clip-show context](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/A-Dressing_Memories)).

## Important moments

All three scenes are from **“The Saddle Row Review” (S6E9)**. Watch the [official full episode](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YHp6wHBGUjk); **scene timestamps unavailable** because their exact positions could not be verified.

1. **A landlord's ultimatum:** Mr. Stripes threatens to raise Rarity's rent beyond what she can afford unless she employs Plaid, turning her grand opening into a crisis.
2. **Defending “spoon clothes”:** When Plaid complains that Applejack rejects her ideas, he immediately sides with his daughter, escalating the boutique's troubles.
3. **A workable compromise:** Applejack later apologizes to Mr. Stripes and proposes using Plaid's spoon-clothing concept for refreshments; the idea helps make the opening distinctive, although no spoken response from him is shown.
